simple.meaning: טְאֵב (ṭᵉʼêb) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to rejoice.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 6:24. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טְאֵב (H2868).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: טְאֵב (ṭᵉʼêb) / H2868 is traced through Daniel 6:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H2868. teeb טְאֵב verb be good ( ᵑ7 Syriac, see Biblical Hebrew טוֺב ); — Pe Perfect 3masculine singular ׳ט , with עַל person Dan 6:24 it was good to him = he was glad (compare בְּאֵשׁ 6:15 ).

occurrences.englishText: The king commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke all their bones in pieces, before they came to the bottom of the den.
